newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac says his policies bearing first fruits.
newsitem.headline: Chirac says his policies bearing first fruits.

text.p: President Jacques Chirac said on Wednesday that French government policies were bearing their first fruits and urged his cabinet to maintain its course in pursuing controversial economic reforms.

"At the moment when our ambitious and rational policies are showing their first results, I ask the government to maintain its course," Chirac said at the start of a weekly cabinet meeting, according to government spokesman Alain Lamassoure.
Chirac's popularity in opinion polls has sunk due to near-record 12.7 percent unemployment and government austerity programmes intended to help France qualify for European monetary union from 1999.
He and Prime Minister Alain Juppe have been urging voters for months to dispel a gloomy mood hanging over the French economy and recognise that reforms were working.
Juppe, who took office in May 1995, declared last March that it was "springtime for France" -- only to see joblessness later increase.
Chirac told his cabinet "to pursue reforms under way with courage and determination and through dialogue and widespread consultation, which will eventually have their full effect", Lamassoure said.
